# BWRAPI

> BWAPI for StarCraft: Remastered 1.23.10 (x64 and x86 games): a library for reading the game state and issuing commands. It provides the BWAPI 4.4 API (C++ through the official BWAPI 4.4 SDK, Python through `bwrapi.bwapi`), a lower-level C ABI 1.0 (`bwrapi.dll`, with .NET and Python bindings), and a launcher that injects BWRAPI into a running game and starts bots. Windows only.

This file is for AI coding agents writing code that uses BWRAPI. Agents changing BWRAPI itself read AGENTS.md (Korean) instead.

## Prerequisites

- Windows 10/11 x64, StarCraft: Remastered 1.23.10 installed and running. The user starts the game and opens a match (for a bot, a custom game against the computer); there is no auto-menu. Another game build returns status UNSUPPORTED_BUILD.
- Python 3.11+ (x64): `pip install bwrapi`. C/C++ without Python: `bwrapi-windows.zip` from https://github.com/moccohello/bwrapi/releases (header, x64/x86 `bwrapi.dll` and `bwrapi.lib`, injector, examples). .NET: `BwrApi.Client.1.0.0.nupkg` from the same page.

## Pick the path

- Python bot (BWAPI 4.4 API): subclass `bwrapi.bwapi.AIModule`, use `Broodwar`; run `python -m bwrapi.bwapi.run bot.py --inject`. [Python SDK guide](https://github.com/moccohello/bwrapi/blob/main/docs/SDK.md), [example](https://github.com/moccohello/bwrapi/blob/main/python/examples/bot.py).
- Existing or new C++ BWAPI 4.4 bot: an x86 AIModule DLL built against BWAPI 4.4.0; run `python -m bwrapi.launcher run <bot>.dll`. [Write a bot in C++](https://github.com/moccohello/bwrapi#write-a-bot-in-c).
- HUD, overlay or analysis tool (read only): C ABI `bwr_open(pid, 0, &s)` from your own process, no injection. [C ABI reference](https://github.com/moccohello/bwrapi/blob/main/docs/C-ABI.md), [C example](https://github.com/moccohello/bwrapi/blob/main/crates/ffi/examples/read_units.c), [.NET example](https://github.com/moccohello/bwrapi/blob/main/dotnet/examples/ObserverQuickstart/Program.cs). Python: `bwrapi.native` (section 6 of the SDK guide).
- Commands without the BWAPI layer: inject `bwrapi.dll` (`bwrapi-inject <pid> <dir>\bwrapi.dll`, or any launcher command), then `bwr_submit` / `bwr_poll_result` from your own process. [Example](https://github.com/moccohello/bwrapi/blob/main/crates/ffi/examples/submit_move.c).
- Drawing (`bwr_draw`) and chat capture (`bwr_capture_chat`) work only in a module running inside the game (`bwr_open_self`): [In-game modules](https://github.com/moccohello/bwrapi/blob/main/docs/C-ABI.md#in-game-modules).

## Verify it works

Without a game, you can check only that code imports, names resolve (`help()`, the `.pyi` stubs, a type checker such as pyright, or compiling against `bwrapi.h`), and that errors are handled (a nonexistent pid gives status GONE). Everything else needs a running game:

- `python -m bwrapi.launcher doctor <bot>` checks files and lists running games with their PIDs and bit widths.
- Server log `bwrapi_bwapi.log` next to the injected server DLL (pip install: `<site-packages>\bwrapi\bin\x64\` or `x86\`); a connected bot logs `client connected mode=sync|async`.
- A bot that draws in `onFrame` shows the text on the game screen.

Only attach to a game the user asked you to use: a reader or bot acts on the running StarCraft they may be playing.

## Pitfalls

- AIModule callbacks: `onStart(self)`, `onFrame(self)`, `onEnd(self, isWinner)`, `onUnitCreate(self, unit)` and the other `onUnit*`, `onSendText(self, text)`, `onReceiveText(self, player, text)`, `onPlayerLeft(self, player)`, `onNukeDetect(self, target)`, `onSaveGame(self, gameName)`.
- Python `bwrapi.bwapi.run` without `--inject` waits for a server that someone else injected.
- Sync mode (default) freezes the game while the bot's `onFrame` runs; keep it short or use `--mode async`.
- A BWAPI command returning true means it was handed to the game, not that it took effect; check later frames. The C ABI returns command results (`bwr_poll_result`).
- `Broodwar` is usable only while a client is connected to a server; units, players and regions exist from the match start (`onStart`).
- "None" values are `None_` on the type namespaces (e.g. `UnitTypes.None_`, `Positions.None_`).
- `supplyUsed()` and `supplyTotal()` are in half units, as in BWAPI, so divide by 2 to show them.
- C ABI cells are raw game values: hit points, shields and energy are in 1/256 units, and supply in half units; unknown cells are the type's sentinel (max for unsigned, min for signed). A table that was not read is NULL. Check the C ABI reference for each column.
- C ABI frames stay valid until `bwr_release`; use a session from one thread. Loop: `bwr_step` (wait) then `bwr_acquire`, read, `bwr_release`.
- C++ AIModule DLLs and BWAPI client programs must be x86 binaries.
- Differences from BWAPI 4.4 behavior: [compatibility notes](https://github.com/moccohello/bwrapi/blob/main/docs/BWAPI-COMPATIBILITY.md).
